content.text:
We need to choose which 2 units to lose (destroy) from list: IDs 7,8 (ships in Port of Pyke), 9 footman in Greywater Watch, 6 knight in Greywater Watch, 37 knight in Greywater Watch.

Goal: preserve ability to hold and capture castle areas. Currently Greyjoy holds castles: pyke (castle stronghold), seagard (no castle), flints-finger (castle), greywater-watch (no castle), moat-cailin (no castle). Actually check: pyke is a stronghold (castle=2). Seagard is no castle. Flints-finger has castle=1. Greywater-watch no castle. Moat-cailin no castle. Gray.

We have units: in Greywater Watch: footman and two knights. In Port of Pyke: two ships.

Ships in a port do not provide transport, but having ships in adjacent sea (Ironman's Bay) would provide transport to/from Pyke. Currently Ironman's Bay has no units. So losing ships reduces ability to transport. However we could still transport via ship bridge? We have no ships elsewhere near Pyke.

We have to consider future moves: potential to attack Iron Islands or other areas. Greyjoy may want to use ships to move knights/footmen from Pyke to other coastal areas via Ironman's Bay and then to other seas like Shipbreaker Bay etc? Actually map: Pyke is adjacent to Ironman's Bay (sea) and also to port-of-pyke (port) and to Seagard (land?) Let's check map: pyke [land; castle=2; home=greyjoy] neighbors: ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke. No land neighbor? So to move land units from Pyke, need ship transport via Ironman's Bay and then to another sea area with a ship, then via ship chain etc. Currently no ships near Pyke.

Ships in the port currently: two ships are in port of Pyke. They can be moved out into Ironman's Bay via March order later, then act as transport. Losing them reduces that ability.

But we also have knights in Greywater Watch (land area). Those knights can march to Moat-cailin (already moved), now to Greywater Watch (currently there). From Greywater Watch, neighboring areas: bay-of-ice, flints-finger, ironmans-bay, sunset-sea, seagard (land). Actually check map: greywater-watch [land; supply=1]: neighbors: bay-of-ice, flints-finger, ironmans-bay, moat-cailin, seagard. So from Greywater Watch we could march knights to seagard (which is our land area, but no castle), or to flints-finger (castle). So knights could be used to capture or defend castle at flints-finger. Footman as well.

Thus losing knights might weaken ability to hold/flank flints-finger, may also affect ability to transport via ship? Knights don't help ship transport. But we might need knights to attack other coastal areas later (like move via ship transport). Having knights in Greywater Watch could later be moved via ship transport if we get ships in Ironman's Bay and then chain to e.g., shipbreaker bay, etc.

Which losses are less harmful? Ships are not currently providing transport, but could later. However we have two ships; losing one still leaves one for transport. Footman is a weaker unit; losing footman vs losing a knight—knight is stronger (2 combat). But we have 2 knights already; losing a knight reduces strength but still have one knight plus footman.

Also we must consider supply limit: we have supply=3, currently units: 2 ships, 1 footman, 2 knights =5 units. Supply limit 3 means we can have armies: per supply track 3 => allowed army sizes: 3,2,2,2 (four armies). But we currently have: ship units count as army if in same sea area: port of pyke has 2 ships -> that's an army of size 2. Greywater Watch land area has 3 units (footman+2 knights) which is an army of size 3. That's within supply (size 3). So total armies 2, both within allowed.

If we lose a ship, we have 1 ship (army size 1) which is not an army (single unit). So supply fine.

If we lose a footman, then Greywater Watch would have 2 knights (size 2) still okay.

If we lose a knight, then Greywater Watch would have footman+ knight = size 2, still okay.

Goal: preserve ability to hold and capture castles. Flints-finger is a castle area we already control (controlPowerToken: greyjoy). It already has our units there (footman and knights). Losing a knight reduces defense there. Losing footman also reduces.

Which is more important? Probably keeping at least one knight in Greywater Watch to defend flints-finger later. Also keep footman maybe less valuable. But knights are stronger combat, so better to keep knights. So maybe sacrifice footman (ID 9) and one ship (ID 7 or 8). That leaves us with one ship for transport, two knights in Greywater Watch for defense/capture.

Thus choose unit_ids_to_destroy = [9,7] (footman and one ship). Could also pick 8, same. Choose 7.

Make sure IDs are distinct and from list.

Return JSON.
